details:
What It Does & How It Works:
"Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" is an interactive digital storytelling web experience designed to bring the journey of NASA’s Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity ("Oppy" / MER-B) to life for young learners. Guided by a friendly young host, visitors move through a visual timeline covering Oppy’s construction at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, its naming by 9-year-old essay contest winner Sofi Collis, its 26-bounce airbag landing inside Eagle Crater on Mars, its discovery of "Martian Blueberries" proving ancient flowing water, its world-record 45.16 km drive across 5,111 Sols (~15 years), and its final dust-storm message from Perseverance Valley. Visitors can listen to expressive narration, inspect an Official NASA Facts Board alongside real NASA Mars archive photos, take an interactive quiz, and write a personal "Letter to Oppy."

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Space science is often presented through dense technical tables that feel overwhelming to school students. This platform bridges the gap between scientific archives and young imaginations by making planetary telemetry emotional, visual, and easy to understand. Its intended impact is to inspire students to explore STEM and space history while ensuring humanity’s bravest abandoned explorers are never forgotten.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

  • Frontend & Hosting: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, deployed live via Netlify.
  • Design & Multimedia: Canva (visual layout and demo presentation), ElevenLabs (expressive voiceover narration), and AI visual generation tools for custom 2D animated character scenes.
  • Data Sources: Verified NASA telemetry and archive imagery from NASA Science (science.nasa.gov/mission/mer-opportunity) and NASA NSSDCA (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov).

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:
Rather than building a static encyclopedia page, we combined character-driven storytelling, emotional audio pacing, and interactive participation (quizzes and letters to Oppy). Working as a solo creator, key factors considered included scientific accuracy, age-appropriate language for young learners, visual accessibility, and strict adherence to NASA data and AI transparency guidelines.
